chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Muskhan, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who becomes junub in the month of Ramadan and forgets this throughout it until the month of Ramadan ends. He said: 'He must make up the prayer and the fasting.'

key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: becomes junub (enters state of major ritual impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who stays in a state of junub throughout Ramadan without making up prayers or fasting?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that forgetting one's state of major impurity (junub) throughout Ramadan exempts the individual from the penalty of *kaffarah* (expiation), requiring only the simple making up (*qada*) of both missed prayers and fasting days. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between intentional and unintentional acts, emphasizing that the omission of *ghusl* does not invalidate the fast if the person was unaware of their state. The hadith underscores the principle of ease in ritual obligations when forgetfulness is the primary factor.
